generations.prompt: Photoreal, 1943, the sidewalk outside a movie theater in flat overcast daylight; the camera stands still at eye height on the sidewalk behind her and does not move. The young woman in the tilted hat and charcoal coat, seen from behind, walks away from the camera toward the brass doors of the theater ahead of her on the left, unhurried, small steady steps, her face lifted to the marquee above her and then lowering toward the doors as she angles toward them; by the end her gloved hand is reaching for the brass door handle. She never turns back to the camera, never stops, never speaks. The man in the hat far down the sidewalk keeps walking at his own pace; the parked car stays parked; the marquee bulbs stay off in the daylight. Deep focus, true colour, no grain, no haze, no slow motion; plain ordinary footage. Sound: a quiet street, her heels on the pavement, one car passing, a distant voice; no music, no dialogue. Exactly the people already in the frame; nobody new enters. No on-screen text, no signs, no lettering anywhere; the marquee board stays blank.
